previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, and prior DVT/PE was admitted for worsening bilateral lower extremity swelling and pain. She had been on outpatient IV clindamycin for cellulitis, which was improving, but her edema persisted. The primary issue was determined to be acute on chronic lymphedema, not infection or heart failure. She was treated with IV furosemide initially, then transitioned to oral bumetanide and spironolactone after a rise in creatinine. Her INR fluctuated due to antibiotic interactions, requiring warfarin dose adjustments and a short Lovenox bridge. Oral candidiasis was treated with fluconazole. A transient rash and chills resolved without identifying a specific drug trigger. Wound care managed weeping skin lesions. By discharge, her swelling and pain had improved, weight decreased, and labs stabilized. She was discharged home with services on optimized diuretic, anticoagulant, and pain regimens, with follow-up plans for sleep study, primary care, and wound monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
Outpatient Providers: Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with a 
history of diastolic heart failure, obesity, lymphedema, 
recurrent deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and recurrent 
cellulitis with a chronic indwelling PICC line, who presented 
with fever, leukocytosis, and worsening right lower extremity 
pain and erythema, concerning for recurrence of cellulitis, 
admitted for antibiotic therapy. 

#Cellulitis
The patient presented with increased swelling, pain, and 
erythema of her right lower extremity, concerning for recurrence 
of cellulitis. The patient has had 6 prior admissions for 
cellulitis in the past ___ years. The cellulitis was without 
abscess formation and there was low concern for necrotizing 
fasciitis. The patient was initially started on IV vancomycin 
and IV clindamycin on admission on ___. There was clinical 
improvement in the cellulitis and the patient was de-escalated 
to PO clindamycin on ___. After transition to PO clindamycin, 
the patient's cellulitis worsened in the setting of significant 
lower extremity edema likely from lymphedema and volume 
overload. Given concern for worsening infection the patient was 
escalated back to IV vancomycin and IV clindamycin on ___ after 
which clindamycin was discontinued on ___. On IV vancomycin, 
the patient's cellulitis showed slow improvement. Given the slow 
response to IV antibiotics, the infectious disease team was 
consulted who recommended continuation of IV vancomycin with 
continued aggressive management of the patient's lower extremity 
edema as described below. Wound care was also consulted to 
address skin protection, positioning, cleaning and wound 
dressing in the area of cellulitis. The patient showed continued 
improvement on IV vanc, though did develop a new focus of pain, 
tenderness, blistering on the upper lateral left calf that was 
felt to be non-infectious cellulitis in setting of her 
lymphedema. IV vancomycin was continued until ___ (day of last 
dose) completing a nearly 2 week course. On ___, the patient 
was transitioned to oral doxycycline 100 mg bid and oral 
cephalexin 500 mg po q6 hours (which she has tolerated in the 
past despite a reported Ceclor allergy) for a planned 10 day 
course (end date ___. 

#Pain 
The patient presented with significant pain in the area of her 
cellulitis. Her pain was managed with her home regimen of 
oxycodone 45mg that was increased to q4h from q6h prn along with 
0.25 mg dilaudid IV q4h (later uptitrated to 0.5 mg) for 
breakthrough pain and standing acetaminophen. The chronic pain 
team was consulted given difficult pain control, hyperalgesia 
and history of fibromyalgia. In addition to outpatient 
management outlined in transitional issues they recommended 
continuation of the above regimen while in the hospital with a 
decrease of IV dilaudid once the infection improved and 
transition to home dose oxycodone and morphine at discharge. On 
___, the patient's IV dilaudid was decreased and she was 
transitioned back to her home morphine in addition to her home 
dose oxycodone q4H PRN. 
-Provided with Rx for narcan
-Overall pain very difficult to control in a patient who has 
chronic narcotic use at large doses (oxycodone 45mg PO Q6hours 
PRN AND morphine 45mg PO Q6hours PRN).  Suggested long acting 
narcotics, which patient declined as noting that she does not 
want to be on consistent medications if she can get away with 
only taking 2 oxycodone per day instead of the 4.  She has 
failed gabapenting/pregabalin in the past due to effects of 
somnolence and reports use of amitriptyline in the past.  
Recommend outpatient weaning of narcotics, initiation of 
antidepressant, and other nonnarcotics pain management routes.

#Chronic Diastolic heart Failure 
#Lymphedema 
The patient has a history of heart failure with preserved 
ejection fraction. The patient has a home regimen of bumex 2mg 
daily and Lasix 80mg IV prn for which she has a chronic PICC in 
place for administration by ___. Prior to admission the patient 
had not been taking her bumex for several days and reported that 
her legs had more edema than baseline. Her lower extremity edema 
was felt to be due to a combination of lymphedema and volume 
overload in the setting of diastolic heart failure. The patient 
was continued on her home spironolactone and ezetimibe on 
admission. She refused to take diuretic therapy during her first 
three days of admission due to pain and unwillingness to walk to 
the bathroom. She started bumex therapy on ___ which was 
transitioned to IV Lasix on ___. A foley was placed given 
patient's increasing pain. She continued to undergo diuresis 
with IV Lasix (80-100mg BID) with improvement in her edema and 
was transitioned to 4mg po bumex QD on ___, and then 2mg po 
bumex QD on ___ per patient request. The patient refused 
referral to a ___ clinic. The patient's admission weight 
was 339.07 lbs and on discharge her weight was 346.21 lbs.
- Discharge Creatinine 1.3.
- Discharge weight 346.21 lbs (157.04 kg)

#Recurrent Deep Vein Thrombosis/Pulmonary Embolism: 
The patient presented with a sub-therapeutic INR at 1.5. Goal 
INR ___. The patient was continued on daily warfarin. On 
discharge, the patient was on 7 mg of warfarin and the INR was 
1.7. She was encouraged to follow up with her PCP regarding 
further warfarin adjustments in light of her antibiotic dosing.

#Clostridium Difficile
Patient had a report of semi-formed stool. A sample was sent and 
the C. difficile DNA amplification assay was positive. However, 
the patient did not have any diarrhea during hospitalization. 
Given the absence of symptoms, the infection was not felt to be 
active and was not treated in accordance with recommendations 
from the infectious disease team. 

#Past Traumatic Experience in Hospital 
The patient reported a traumatic event during a previous 
hospitalization in which she was intubated and given paralytics 
without sedation. She reported occasional flashbacks of the 
event in the hospital and noted trouble sleeping in the hospital 
because of the event. The benefits of a psychiatric consultation 
were discussed with the patient, but she declined.
